summary: A 1961 CL-100 cab on a 55-foot steel tower above the Stanislaus National Forest, the third lookout structure on this Tuolumne County summit since at least 1925.

facts.design: USFS National Plan CL-100 cab on a 55-foot K-Brace steel tower (built 1961)

staffing.note: Per NHLR, staffed daily during fire season by the Forest Service

facts.agency: Stanislaus National Forest, Mi-Wok Ranger District

events.note: Original lookout: a 60' "windmill type" tower with a flat, unroofed platform, in place by at least 1925
Second structure: 40' steel tower with a 7'x7' cab, plus an adjacent wooden residence, replacing the 1925 windmill tower
Current CL-100 cab on a 55' K-Brace steel tower, replacing the 1931 structure
Registered April 24, 2017; nominated by Bill Luedeke

notes_for_editor: Design history (three successive structures, 1925/1931/1961) is well documented by NHLR, but no source gives named keepers, specific fires spotted, or a current staffing/access status beyond NHLR's general 'staffed daily during fire season' line, which is undated and may be stale. NHLR's descriptive paragraph also mentions 'Mi-Wok Ranger District, 4,939' elevation' separately from the page's stated lookout elevation of 4,931 ft; this reads like boilerplate district text rather than a conflicting lookout elevation, so no correction is proposed.
